faculty.name: Anjana Mudambi
faculty.title: Associate Professor; Undergraduate Program Director
research_areas: Identity construction, discursive reproduction, and agency among South Asian Americans
Systems of power and anti-racist solidarity
faculty.bio: Dr. Mudambi is a critical qualitative intercultural communication scholar. In her research, she seeks to challenge the systems of power that position cultural communities in relation to each other, improve communication and pedagogy about race within the university, and help expand the application of critical perspectives in the field of communication. For more information about her, her teaching, and her scholarship, please visit her website. Please note that she is on sabbatical for the 2026-2027 academic year. From her personal site: her research focuses on identity construction, discursive reproduction, and agency among South Asian Americans and on systems of power; she has explored constructions of brownness across Latinx and South Asian American immigrant communities and conceptualized critically reflexive racialization as a way for marginalized communities to engage in anti-racist discourse and interracial solidarity. Research on Critical Intercultural Communication Pedagogy (CICP) is an important part of her scholarship. Current projects include a qualitative study of students from conservative backgrounds in CICP-informed courses, an ethnographic study of sub-Saharan African immigrants in Turkey, and a monograph project on second-generation South Asian Americans' engagement in social justice. faculty.name: Erin Parcell
faculty.title: Professor
faculty.bio: Research interests: Professor Parcell's research currently centers on communication within and about interpersonal and family relationships. A primary area of her work focuses on long-distance relationships, including college dating couples and deployed military marriages/families. She most often employs qualitative methods for her research (e.g., in-depth interviews) but has participated in several meta-analyses and survey design studies. A secondary area for Professor Parcell's work focuses on gun violence in southeastern Wisconsin, in particular the stories community members share about their experiences. She is on an interdisciplinary team seeking to address this issue by, in part, helping to elevate the voices of gun violence survivors via our living archive . She encourages students, both graduate and undergraduate, as well as community members to contact me if they are interested in participating in my existing projects or to start new ones. Selected publications: Suter, E. A., Sahlstein Parcell, E., Adebayo, C. T., Romo, D. C., & Weadlock, C. R. (2024). faculty.name: Lia Wolock
faculty.title: Assistant Professor
faculty.bio: From her personal site: My research and teaching explore the racialization of minority and transnational communities in the age of digital and social media, with a focus on the South Asian American diaspora and its media activism. I've written on South Asian Americans' shifting position in US racial politics and the community's responses to being historically misrepresented and underrepresented, media representations of India and Indian American identities (MTV-Desi and Outsourced), and the creative labor that activists take on to build new racial justice-oriented solidarities (Sepia Mutiny, the South Asian American Digital Archive). My current book project, Producing South Asian America: Diaspora, Race, and Digital Activism, examines the emergence of a new North American racial identity, and the media sites and labor that undergird it. PhD in Communication Studies and MA in South Asian Studies, University of Michigan. CV lists research and teaching interests as Race, Diaspora, & Digital Media; Media Activism & Production; South Asia & United States. Selected publications: Wolock, Lia. “Diaspora and Digital Media” Race and Media: Critical Approaches New York, New York: New York University Press. (2020): 190-201. | Wolock, Lia, and Punathambekar, Aswin. “Race and Ethnicity in Post-network American Television” Television and New Media 16.7 Ed. Mayer, Vicki. (2015): 664–679.
